transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-07
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Tom (Copperleaf Eng Mgr), Maya (Product), Samir (SRE), Leah (Security)

Summary:
- Copperleaf is evaluating whether to run on Redwood Hosted initially, then move to Dedicated or Private for regulated workloads. Primary concerns are p95 latency for streaming chat (target 150-250ms token latency), steady-state concurrency, and token/sec throughput for nightly bulk jobs.
- They want a short benchmark run with their prompt set to validate p95 and token/sec numbers and to see fallback behavior under capacity constraints.
- Security/compliance gating is SOC2 + KMS + VPC peering details; Leah will share questionnaire answers.

Topics:
- p95 streaming latency targets and how Redwood measures p95 vs tail spikes
- Dedicated vs Hosted economics at high concurrency
- KV cache/prefix caching behavior for chat sessions
- Quantization options and effect on tokens/sec
- Private (VPC/on-prem) network considerations and audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
[00:07] Tom (Copperleaf): Yeah Tom here, I run the inference infra team. Maya is our product lead and Samir does SRE, Leah is security.
[00:15] Maya: Hi all. We're mainly evaluating latency and whether we go Hosted or Dedicated for initial launch.
[00:23] Priya (Redwood SE): Great. Two quick clarifying questions: what's your p95 target for user-visible streaming tokens, and what's your expected steady concurrency?
[00:31] Samir: For chat UI we want p95 per-token latency <250ms ideally 150ms. Concurrency wise, we expect 250 active concurrent sessions during peak with an average 3 tokens/sec per session. For nightly batch embed jobs it's a different axis — we're looking at sustained 20k tokens/sec across workers.
[00:49] Jonah (Redwood): Okay makes sense. Just to translate: for streaming that means roughly 750 tokens/sec aggregate at peak for interactive, bursts higher. For the batch pipeline we should look at throughput-focused nodes or dedicated pools.
[01:02] Priya: Also do you have requirements for cold start or KV cache hit rates? If you can get high cache hit rates for ongoing sessions it changes the p95 story a lot.
[01:12] Tom: We do have session affinity at the app layer, but some users hit multiple devices so KV misses occur ~30% on average.
[01:20] Maya: Another thing, we have HIPAA-like constraints for some customers. Our compliance folks prefer private deployments eventually. For MVP we could consider Hosted if we have contractual SLAs and audit logs.
[01:31] Leah (Security): Yes, SOC2 is non-negotiable, SSO/SAML + KMS integration expected, and we want audit logs retained for 90 days. Can Redwood support HSM-backed KMS in private mode?
[01:43] Alex: Short answer yes for Private we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For Hosted we provide envelope encryption and offer a bring-your-own-key flow for enterprise tiers; we'll follow up with the security pack.
[01:55] Samir: On capacity, what does Dedicated look like? If we reserve Dedicated pools, can we handle 20k sustained tokens/sec plus bursts to 60k for pipeline replays?
[02:06] Priya: Dedicated pools let you reserve a number of GPUs with predictable throughput. Throughput depends on model family and quantization. For example, for a 13B dense model on A100-style nodes we typically see ~200-400 tokens/sec per GPU in generation, but that's very workload dependent. With INT8-ish quantization we can often get 2x throughput. For streaming small tokens p95 is usually dominated by scheduling latency unless you use continuous batching and prefix KV caching.
[02:33] Tom: Curious, what about the p95 tail during high burst? How does Redwood handle graceful degradation?
[02:40] Jonah: We do routing policies: canary to cheaper model variants, fall back to smaller model family when capacity is tight, and we have auto-burst queues for short spikes. That can add latency, but keeps the app live. We can also route by region to avoid cross-region hops.
[02:54] Maya: We need concrete numbers. Can Redwood run our prompt set and show p95 and token/sec curves?
[02:59] Priya: Absolutely — ideal next step is a short benchmark run. If you share a representative prompt corpus (5-10k prompts, plus average seq lengths) we can run 2 workloads: streaming chat (simulate 250 concurrent sessions) and bulk (sustained token-speed test). We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and per-token latency, as well as GPU util and KV hit effect.
[03:18] Samir: Timeline?
[03:20] Alex: We'll aim to start the bench next week once we get prompt set and auth. Priya can run it and dump logs to the shared bench link.
[03:27] Leah: On security we need to see the SOC2 report and demo of KMS integration; also an architecture diagram for Private deployment.
[03:35] Alex: We'll send SOC2 + ISO pack and Private deployment guide. Also include audit log retention options and SAML SSO docs.
[03:41] Tom: Cost is important. If Dedicated is much more expensive than Hosted, we might go hybrid: Hosted for general traffic, Dedicated for sensitive customers. How do you price capacity?
[03:49] Jonah: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved monthly with an expected throughput. We'll share a matrix showing cost-per-1k-tokens at different batch sizes and expected p95 tradeoffs. Also examples of mixed-routing policies.
[03:59] Maya: A couple of nitty-gritty questions — what about quantization-related quality degradation? We care about hallucination rates on long context.
[04:08] Priya: We monitor generation quality on eval prompt sets. Quantization can slightly affect logits, but for most instruction-style prompts the delta is minor. We'll run your evals as part of the bench and report any quality regressions. We also support A/B rollouts and automatic fallback to full-precision models if quality dips.
[04:24] Samir: Networking: if we do Private in our VPC, how's traffic routed? We need low-latency egress to our services and encrypted peering.
[04:33] Alex: Private offers VPC peering and an on-prem package. We'll include an example network architecture. For VPC peering the latency is essentially your intra-region network plus minimal processing; we can quantify that in the bench.
[04:43] Leah: For audit we need immutable logs with user-ids and tokens redacted. Is that supported?
[04:48] Jonah: Yes, audit logs are plumbed; we redact PII by config, and retention windows are configurable per account.
[04:56] Tom: Back to numbers — you said 200-400 tokens/sec/GPU for 13B. For our nightly batch we need 20k sustained tokens/sec. Roughly how many GPUs would that be?
[05:05] Priya: If we assume 300 tokens/sec/GPU, that's ~67 GPUs sustained. With quantization 2x you'd be ~33 GPUs. But batch efficiency also depends on seq length — shorter sequences are higher tokens/sec. We'll surface GPU counts in the bench report.
[05:19] Samir: Good. How about streaming p95 — do you have examples of p95 token latency when concurrency is high and KV misses are 30%?
[05:27] Priya: From past runs, with continuous batching and cache hit ~70%, p95 token latency for small tokens was ~120-180ms on Dedicated pools for 13B models. Hosted numbers vary by tier, but enterprise tiers with reserved capacity can match Dedicated latency. We'll include a table of historical runs.
[05:44] Maya: We also have a requirement: 99th percentile of request completion time for short replies (<64 tokens) must be <1.2s. Can Redwood meet that?
[05:53] Jonah: That maps to p99 token and end-to-end scheduling — on Dedicated with correct autoscaling and burst capacity yes; Hosted can too with enterprise committed capacity. We'll validate with your workload.
[06:03] Tom: If we start on Hosted and later move to Private, what's the migration path? Any downtime?
[06:09] Alex: We support pinning model versions and have a blue/green style rollout. Migration planning usually involves exporting model checkpoints (if using private model), but for our managed catalog it's a config change plus data-plane switch. We'll work with your infra team during migration to minimize downtime.
[06:22] Samir: Do you provide token-level cost breakdown in the console? We want per-route cost to reason about feature flags.
[06:28] Jonah: Yes, Console has token-level breakdown and route/model dashboards; you can instrument per-route costs and set alerts. We'll give you a quick demo if helpful.
[06:36] Maya: Please do. For the bench harness, what format do you need prompts in?
[06:41] Priya: JSONL with fields: prompt, expected_len, session_id (for streaming simulation). Also please include a small set of long-context items so we can measure seq-length-related regressions.
[06:50] Tom: We'll prepare that. Also one more ask: can Redwood simulate network jitter to see effects on token latency? Our mobile clients have variable network.
[06:59] Priya: We can add simulated latency at the client emulator. We'll annotate results accordingly.
[07:05] Leah: Security Q — do you support ephemeral certs for the Private agent and how are credentials rotated?
[07:11] Alex: Yes ephemeral certs and automated rotation via your KMS/HSM. We'll include the rotation policy doc.
[07:18] Maya: Great. Anything else on routing policies?
[07:21] Jonah: Just that we can route by policy: minimize latency, minimize cost, or regional affinity. You can create fallback rules to smaller models to keep latency bounded under overload.
[07:31] Tom: Let's recap next steps and owners.
[07:34] Alex: Recap: Alex to send pricing + Hosted vs Dedicated matrix and security pack; Priya to run benchmark using your JSONL prompts and share raw logs + summary; Leah to send completed compliance questionnaire; and we'll reconvene after bench results.
[07:49] Maya: Sounds good. Can we aim to review results the week of 2027-07-19?
[07:54] Alex: Yes, timeline looks fine.
[07:58] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[08:00] Meeting end.
